newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia says plans changes to Native Title.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia says plans changes to Native Title.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday the government would reveal substantial amendments to the Native Titles Act in just over a week's time.

Speaking at a Liberal Party luncheon in Perth, Howard said the amendments would not undermine the basic principles of the act or of the High Court decision on native title (the "Mabo" decision). "But they will address the issue of workability," he said. "They will address the legitimate concerns of many people in the mining and pastoral industry," he said.

"They are designed to try and achieve a fair balance between the rights and interests of Aboriginal people who saw in the Mabo decision a vindication of their long held view about their rights as fellow Australians, and also the legitimate rights of those who seek to risk their capital and their all to develop this country and provide jobs for themselves and for others," Howard said.
"It will be legislation that looks very much to the future so far as relations between Australians are concerned, whether they be Aboriginal or not," Howard said.
